basics.name: Julia Youssef
basics.label: Geophysical Sciences graduate
basics.summary: Geophysical Sciences graduate focused on quantitative paleobiology, macroevolution, and ecological niche evolution through time; integrating morphological, ecological, and stratigraphic data; scientific communication and visualization

education.area: Geophysical Sciences, Honors in Major. Minor: Astronomy & Astrophysics
courses: Coursework Highlights: Phylogenetics in the Fossil Record, Biodiversity, Global Biogeochemical Cycles, Geobiology, Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy, Invertebrate Paleobiology & Evolution
Honors & Scholarships: QuestBridge NCM Finalist, Odyssey Scholar, National Merit Scholar

projects.name: Pterosaur Phylogenetics – manuscript in progress
highlights: Investigated whether persistent disagreements among pterosaur phylogenetic hypotheses produced by semi-independent datasets persist when reanalyzed under standardized parsimony and Bayesian approaches

Designed analysis workflow that restructures and standardizes published morphological datasets, relates taxa with PBDB occurrence records for use in tip-dated tree models or stratigraphic metric measures and processes resulting tree samples for reproducible cross-dataset and cross-method comparisons
Developed robust TNT tree-search script and specified model assumptions, prior distributions, and analysis settings for RevBayes

Quantified changes in topological agreement across dataset x method combinations using pairwise Generalized Robinson-Foulds distances (following Llabres et al. 2023), visualized in tree space; stratigraphic congruence metrics used as complementary measure
Generated representative median trees by minimizing Kendall-Colijn distances to compare the specific clade arrangements across dataset x method combinations

projects.name: Quantitative Ecology of Mammalian Herbivores
highlights: Investigated how mammalian diet can be represented as a multivariate ecological trait for cross-taxon comparison, beyond broad browser—grazer or herbivory—carnivory continua.

Constructed dietary classes to capture variation in consumed items across primary ecological studies on mammalian herbivores, manually scoring ~100 studies spanning ~30 taxa into a ranked diet matrix; applied polychoric PCA and Jaccard clustering to evaluate whether the resultant structure resembled intuitive consumer dietary guilds

Compiled and minimally standardized author-reported dietary items for use in correspondence analysis, identifying both rare and commonly used dietary terms and producing an alternative representation of taxon dietary niches.

Identified limitations in comparing dietary niches in extant herbivores arising from heterogeneous terminology, measurements, author-defined food categories, and inconsistent reporting of ecological context and dietary item importance

Developing a structured ecological-data framework for manual- and “human-in-the-loop” AI-assisted literature extraction, formatting taxon, dietary item, qualifiers, and source evidence into standardized versions for cross-study or downstream comparative analyses
Extending this framework, characterizing diet as a multivariate ecological trait for use in inference with dental morphology across extant and fossil mammals

Assisted with public-facing lab activities and open houses following lab move; painted and helped sculpt models and casts for display, outreach, and donor gifts.

work.name: Webster Lab
highlights: Performed delicate cleaning, staining, mounting, and photography of dozens of fragile, siliceous, mm-scale eodiscid trilobite cranidia for use in geometric morphometric and biostratigraphic analyses

work.name: Deep Skies Lab

Developed and tested regression, classification, and generally machine learning techniques for simulated astrophysical data; presented project methods and rationale to Deep Skies collaborators and Fermilab researchers
